inicio.kicker: LOOP-R Engineering Track · course 1 of 6 · 8 lessons
inicio.titulo: Verification and Evals: whoever says it's done can't be the one who did it
inicio.lead: A separate, skeptical evaluator, a criterion you can check by command, frozen tests, shortcut detection, a golden set, a calibrated judge, metrics that don't fool you, and a layered gate for your loop. All with small scripts you run first for free, with a fake agent and a fake judge.
inicio.capa_alt: Night inspection bench with an articulated magnifier over a board, an oscilloscope, and a terminal in the background.

numeros.t: scripts in the kit, all with a no-cost rehearsal

inicio.aulas_sub: In the order you build the gate: separate who checks, check the criterion, protect the judge, hunt shortcuts, measure with evals and a judge, read the numbers, and put it all together.

itens: People who already use Claude Code or Codex in the terminal and have already heard "done, all tests pass" when they didn't.
People who will leave a loop running on its own and need a judge the agent can't fool.
People who want to compare two versions of an agent with a number, not an impression.

blocos.t: What you'll be able to do
itens: Run a separate evaluator that doesn't read the agent's report and fails what only looks done.
Freeze the tests and everything pytest reads, and catch the agent that deletes, skips, or memorizes the answer.
Build a golden set with regression and a model judge calibrated against your own labels.
Read pass@k, pass^k, variance, and benchmarks without being fooled, and close with a layered gate.
Linux or macOS with git, Python 3, and pytest. The rehearsals don't call any model.
Claude Code or Codex signed in through your subscription, only for the steps marked "real".
Recommended: course 0 (Base) for the done-criterion scale. Course 2 (Long Execution) uses this gate.
